I've been a Zildjian guy all of my life. I love the sounds of the A Customs.

I've been watching a lot of cool drummers use Meinl cymbals, and have started to love the sound of them.

Anyways...what is your preferred cymbal brand and why?

I think all the brands have great offerings. I've owned Zildjians, Sabians, and Paistes over the years and added a couple Dream cymbals to the collection recently, and there's some Meinl on my wish list too.

The Zildjians As (Avedis) has always been one of my favorites- great traditional sounding cymbals- the various Ks are all great if you've got the cash and the A Customs are great crashes and you can't go wrong with a sweet ride. The K Custom Hybrids are pretty sweet, I picked up a 20" ride that's been a great work horse for live stuff. ZXTs are pretty great for a budget cymbal and I actually backlined some of the new ZBTs a couple weeks ago and they were pretty ok, way better than they used to be.

The Sabian HHXs are awesome and I still think the AA/AAX crashes are some of the best sounding crashes for the money. Their XS20 line sounds great too for a budget cymbal and the OMNIs are nice although I haven't tried out the new HHX OMNI. I'm curious to check out some of the Big Ugly rides in person too.

I haven't owned as many Paiste's, but I've backlined quite a few, the 602, 2002, and Giant Beats are all super solid, and their Signature and Master series are top choice. I'm not as big a fan of the Rude and PSTs, but they've got some cool stuff in there too.

Meinl is definitely one of the hottest newcomers, everything I've played from the Byzance line has been amazing, I really dig the Bennie Greb and Mike Johnston cymbals, but haven't bought anything from them yet.

I picked up a Dream Vintage Bliss 22" and a Contact Low Bell Flat Ride 24" and have been very impressed with them. The Vintage Bliss is papery thin and dry, has a great light sounding ping and a china-y wash, great for quieter gigs and practices, never overpowers the room with white noise. The low bell flat ride has an amazing ping, really cool, unique sounding ride, but the crash is a little gong-y. For the price, I think they're tough to beat.

Other than that I've played some stand out Bosphorous and Istanbul cymbals that were smooth as butter. Haven't ever checked out Soultone or TRX in person.

TL;DR: It's tough to pick a favorite, I kinda love them all, ha.

As a college student on a budget, I'm a big fan of Dream cymbals--in my experience, they're great and distinctive sounding cymbals which cost half as much as cymbals from the major brands. I wouldn't recommend them for all situations and players (they're probably not the best for super loud/crashy playing) but they work for me. But really, there are a whole lot of great cymbals out there. It would be boring if everyone played with the same cymbals :)
I know. I love the variations. But damn, there are so many to choose from.

While I'm not brand-loyal, I do have a few favorite lines across the board.

Zildjian K Dark Crashes:

I don't actually own any, but I've used these quite a bit. The Zildjian K Dark Crashes offer an incredibly solid dark crash sound. They're dark and smooth enough for jazz and acoustic work, but they also sound just as good for amplified music. Unlike a lot of dark cymbals on the market, these have a clean crispness, rather than a more trashy wash. Very versatile.

21" Sabian HHX Groove Ride:

This is my go-to ride for everything. It has a little bit of everything. If you hit it midway between the edge and the bell, it has strong, but not piercing definition. If you hit it a little closer to the edge, it has a smoother, dark wash. Strike it on the edge, and you have a huge, surprisingly crisp crash.

14" Paiste Signature Dark Crisp Hi Hats:

I have been eyeing Paistes for a while, and finally pounced on a pair of Dark Crisp Hats. These aren't crisp in the way that New Beats are crisp. Rather than a pinpoint "tick" sound, these hats give out an almost crunchy sound, even when tight. I would describe it as just a little bit dirty, but still clean and refined. These hats lie a little bit on the loud side, but their dark sound blends very nicely, balancing out the sound.

Overall, I prefer dark cymbals over bright cymbals. I like to blend, rather than cut through music. But I don't want my cymbals to be so dark or trashy that my nuances are lost in the mix.

I love every Istanbul Agop cymbal I've heard played. As far as what I own, I have a set of hats and a crash from Bosphorus that I really dig and a Zildjian K 24" Light Ride that is one of my favorite cymbals I've ever played.

Out of the "Big 4" cymbal manufacturers, I would buy Zildjian K's or their newer Kerope line. But even within the K line there's some I don't like and would never purchase blind. I would need to play everything a few times first before sinking any money into a purchase. As far as the other three, every Sabian I've ever played I have hated. A few Meinl's I've liked. Paiste's sound good but they aren't really the sound I've ever been looking for.

Zildjian my whole life. Started on the more affordable A series, and now that im able to afford what I want I am onto K Dark and Custom. What can I say, Im a complex guy, lol That doesn't mean I dont like other brands, but they just dont offer the same versitility IMO.
